references.text: The contrast to the curse - The Lord will make you the head and not the tail when you keep His commands; here we see the opposite in verse 44
The promise that Israel will lend to many nations and borrow from none, which stands in contrast to the curse of having to borrow
Foreigners have taken over the inheritance of the Israelites, showing the fulfillment of the curse of being the tail and not the head
The Lord will cut off both head and tail from Israel in one day; the image of head and tail is used to refer to leaders and those who are led
Lender and borrower shall share the same fate - referring to the economic aspect of the curse
The people must buy their own water and firewood, a sign of economic inferiority as described in the curse
